title: Today's top defense-tech headlines
big: 34 new stories since the last brief. The busiest areas: allies & theaters and drones & air autonomy.

stories.h: Elbit wins $260 million PULS rocket artillery deal from NATO
stories.what: Israeli defense company Elbit Systems has won a contract worth about $260 million to supply PULS rocket artillery launchers and munitions to an unnamed NATO country in Europe, the company said Thursday.
stories.you: More of the military's sensing and communications now runs through orbit, and new suppliers are getting in.

stories.h: Plans To Fly Talon Blue CCA Drone From British Carrier Confirmed By Northrop Grumman
stories.what: The Royal Navy wants to infuse drone capabilities into its air wings and Talon Blue would be far more advanced than anything that has flown off the carriers yet.
stories.you: Drones are becoming the military's default purchase, so volume, price and reliability decide who wins.

stories.h: EU sets out $3.4B defense budget for 2027, boosts Ukraine spending
stories.what: The new fiscal uplift comes in the wake of Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy telling European leaders last month that “we need at least €70 billion more from you.”
stories.you: Budget and policy moves decide which programs get real money and when; they're the earliest signal of demand.

stories.h: Space Force, UT Austin Open BMC3I TAP Lab Texas for Early-Stage Space Domain Awareness Software
stories.what: BMC3I TAP Lab Texas will be led by astrodynamicist Moriba Jah and operate within UT Austin's Cockrell School of Engineering.
stories.you: Software that decides what to look at and what to hit is where the most value is moving.

stories.h: NATO nations have a missile crisis. How did it happen, and can it be fixed?
stories.what: Breaking Defense kicks off a new video roundtable series about the future of missiles and missile defense.
stories.you: Weapons stockpiles are short, so anyone who can make missiles and rocket motors faster and cheaper has buyers.

watch.h: Stopgap funding expires: FY27 appropriations or another CR
watch.why: December 11. Decides whether DAWG's $54.6B and Golden Dome's growth become real money.

idea.why: Sensor fusion and attribution software (RF, radar, acoustic, camera) for bases, data centers, stadiums, prisons and utilities. $14.4B FY27 counter-UAS line plus the base-defense pilot. Commercial sites legally can only detect and report drones, so software is what they buy.
